author: blu
body: The registry tier of peer discovery. `cdx-serve` answers "give me the work with hash X"; this answers "who has it", which is the question an asker holding only a digest actually has. Until now a peer had to be NAMED -- `compile.ps1 -Peer host:port` -- so a work could only be fetched between two parties already introduced. This is the introduction.

author: blu
body: Announcing inverts it. The peer dials the registry at BOOT, when it has nothing inbound open, so nothing nests at either end. The registry answers every locate out of memory. The nesting is not avoided by careful sequencing; it is unreachable.

author: blu
body: The registry takes NO configuration. It learns its peers by being told.

author: blu
body: The reply carries a `from` and it is empty, which is the honest value. Nothing checks it -- a signed rumour is still a rumour, and the check that protects the asker happens after the fetch, against the content. `cdx-serve` fills its own in because it answers with content; there is nothing here for a key to attest.

author: blu
body: codex-vm's NAT constants, spelled here for the reason `cdx-serve` spells them: they belong in `NetworkStack` with the NIC's own addresses and they are not there yet.

author: blu
body: A tag that is neither a locate nor an announcement is dropped rather than answered. This is not a peer and does not serve works, so a work-request arriving here gets nothing back and the connection closes.

author: blu
body: The margin is a WINDOW and both edges have been measured. Too long and this server stays blocked on a silent connection while the caller that matters is dropped for want of an accept; too short and it abandons a live client before its request arrives.
